problem:
Suppose that for the angles $u$ and $v,$ we have 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡u=\frac{3}{5},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u=\frac{4}{5},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v=\frac{15}{17}.
$$

Given that $v$ lies in the first quadrant, find the value of $\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v).$
worked_solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

We know the values of $\operatorname{sin}⁡u$, $\operatorname{cos}⁡u$, and $\operatorname{cos}⁡v.$ To find the missing value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡v,$ we can use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡v+{cos}^{2}⁡v=1\,⟹\,{sin}^{2}⁡v=1-{cos}^{2}⁡v
$$

Substituting our values into the Pythagorean identity, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡v & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡v \\  & =1-{(\frac{15}{17})}^{2} \\  & =1-\frac{{15}^{2}}{{17}^{2}} \\  & =1-\frac{225}{289} \\  & =\frac{289}{289}-\frac{225}{289} \\  & =\frac{64}{289}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{64}{289}} \\  & =\pm \frac{8}{17}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $v$ lies in the first quadrant, where sine is positive. So, we disregard the negative value, and we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡v=\frac{8}{17}.
$$

We can now apply the difference formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\  & =(\frac{4}{5})(\frac{15}{17})+(\frac{3}{5})(\frac{8}{17}) \\  & =\frac{60}{85}+\frac{24}{85} \\  & =\frac{84}{85}\end{aligned}
$$
